clue.text: Stumble before the French start event

parts.note: to stumble is to trip
le is the French masculine word for 'the'
to start in fright is to jump

explanation.surface: A competitor trips up before a race in France gets under way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' looks like the beginning of the event, but it is the verb meaning to jump in surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: This hop, step and jump is a field discipline in athletics meetings.

clue.text: Foot of column found beneath salt lake

indicators.note: found beneath places the letter below the sailor in this down answer

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, as is a tar

indicators.note: in a down clue the foot of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The base of a pillar is found under a salt lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salt' is the sailor, not the adjective describing the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarn is a small mountain lake, especially in the English Lake District.

clue.text: Popular one-time source of session singers

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
former means one-time or previous

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

explanation.surface: A trendy ex-supplier of backing vocalists for recording sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: To sing is slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang, to sing is to grass to the police, so informers are singers.

clue.text: Says I'm thick, when I'm not well?

definitions.text: Says I'm thick, when I'm not well?

parts.words: Says I'm thick, when I'm not well?
parts.note: someone with this speech defect pronounces S as TH, so 'I'm sick' comes out as 'I'm thick'

explanation.surface: A patient complains of feeling stupid while ill.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth Bott in the Just William books famously talks this way.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisping means pronouncing the S sound as TH, which turns 'sick' into 'thick'.

clue.text: This may be launched and broadcast live in January

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the month's abbreviation
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A TV show is launched and aired live in the new year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' makes AVELI; 'This' stands for the answer, which is thrown in a field event rather than aired.
explanation.definitionFit: A javelin is a spear thrown in athletics, so it is launched through the air.

clue.text: Mother left Fat Duck

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
lard is pig fat

explanation.surface: A mother leaves the Fat Duck, Heston Blumenthal's famous restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fat Duck is a celebrated restaurant in Bray, Berkshire; here 'Fat' and 'Duck' do separate jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: The mallard is the common wild duck with a green-headed drake.

clue.text: Buttonhole constituent on the way back

indicators.note: travelling the way back means the word for constituent is read from right to left

parts.note: a constituent is a part of a whole

explanation.surface: Looks like a description of a flower worn in a lapel by a voter heading home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buttonhole' is the verb: to waylay someone and keep them talking.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttonhole someone is to accost and detain them, much as one might catch or snare them.

clue.text: Rear section of orchestra is effective

indicators.note: section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: The back row of the orchestra is doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear' looks like the back of the orchestra, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To rear children or animals is to bring them up, to raise them.

clue.text: Attractive of course, and quite certain

parts.note: pretty means attractive
sure is an informal reply meaning of course

explanation.surface: Someone is confident that a thing is good-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pretty sure is being fairly confident, nearly convinced.

clue.text: Left, accepting bishop is yet to lose

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the bishop goes inside the word for left

parts.note: food left on the plate is uneaten
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A chess game where the bishop is accepted and the player hasn't lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' is leftover food, not the direction.
explanation.definitionFit: An unbeaten team or player has not been defeated so far.

clue.text: Floats a good deal

definitions.meaning: flat timber platforms that float on water

explanation.surface: A shopper describes some floats as a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple log platforms used as floats on water; informally, rafts of things means lots of them.

clue.text: Sweetheart from Vienna let off

indicators.note: off suggests something gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lover is released from the Austrian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges VIENNA LET.
explanation.definitionFit: A valentine is a beloved person, the one you send a card to on 14 February.

clue.text: City supporters suffer returning after international

indicators.note: after places the reversed piece behind the abbreviation for international

parts.note: bras are supporting undergarments

indicators.note: returning means the word for suffer is read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to suffer illness

explanation.surface: A city's football fans endure a comeback after an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporters' are underwear here, not fans; 'returning' gives LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The purpose-built capital of Brazil, a modernist city laid out in the 1950s.

clue.text: Upstanding before court

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Someone of good character appears before a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: Upstanding in its literal sense is standing straight up, upright.

clue.text: Shunned escort, said to be upset

indicators.note: to be upset means to be knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A companion was snubbed and is said to be distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' looks like a link to the next phrase, but it is part of the fodder ESCORT SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ostracised is to be excluded from a group, cold-shouldered by society.

clue.text: The girl remained in drinking place

parts.note: she is the pronoun for a girl
'I've been in all day' means I remained indoors

explanation.surface: A woman stayed put in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: A shebeen is an unlicensed Irish or Scottish drinking den.
explanation.definitionFit: A shebeen is an illicit bar or unlicensed pub, especially in Ireland, Scotland or South Africa.

clue.text: Forever holding vote outside

indicators.note: holding means the word for forever has the cross placed within it

parts.note: eternal means lasting forever
a cross, X, marks a vote on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A permanent vote takes place out of doors.
explanation.definitionFit: External describes what is on the outer side, exterior.

clue.text: Lists features

definitions.meaning: to detail is to itemise or list, so this is the verb form

explanation.surface: A short phrase about catalogue entries describing characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail things is to itemise them; details are small individual points or characteristics.

clue.text: I left American soldier in pub not making sense

indicators.note: in places the soldier inside the word for pub

parts.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
a GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a US serviceman in a bar, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'local' is British slang for the pub nearest your home.
explanation.definitionFit: Illogical reasoning is irrational and lacks sound sense.

clue.text: Endless danger comes with German chap offering dish of rice

indicators.note: endless means the word for danger loses its final letter

parts.note: risk means danger
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German man offers an Italian dish that is perilous to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian preparation of arborio grains cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Newspaper article covering unknown material

indicators.note: covering means the newspaper and article enclose the unknown

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or publication speaking for a group
a is the indefinite article
in algebra Z is an unknown quantity

explanation.surface: A press report covers a mystery fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts Z between ORGAN and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Organza is a thin, stiff, sheer fabric, typically of silk.

clue.text: Police dog must have one name, right?

parts.note: handle is informal for a person's name

explanation.surface: A query about whether a police dog needs its own name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' is slang for a name, as in a CB radio handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Every police dog works with an officer who trains and controls it.

clue.text: Half-term perhaps finding one in embrace with a Yankee

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the word for embrace

parts.note: to hold someone is to embrace them
I is the Roman numeral for one
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A school break spent hugging an American.
explanation.walkthrough: A half-term is a short school break in the middle of a British school term.
explanation.definitionFit: Half-term is an example of a school vacation, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Spring may be better here, without limits

parts.note: to cap something is to better or outdo it

indicators.note: without limits means the outer letters of here are dropped, keeping the centre

explanation.surface: Someone suggests the spring weather may be an improvement here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is the verb meaning outdo, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful skip or leap, so to spring about is to caper.

clue.text: Tried to impress and modelled

definitions.meaning: to pose is to put on airs to impress others
a model ... for an artist or photographer

explanation.surface: A vain model showing off on a photoshoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Posing means behaving affectedly to impress, and also sitting or standing for a portrait.

clue.text: Lends gig tailored for horses?

indicators.note: tailored means cut and reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone lends a carriage adapted for horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailored' rearranges LENDS GIG; the question mark flags that geldings are only one kind of horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Geldings are castrated male horses, so the plural answer is an example of horses.

clue.text: Fresh air and rising intelligence of Asian

indicators.note: fresh means new or remade, so these letters are rearranged
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the measure of intelligence is reversed

parts.note: IQ is the measure of intelligence

explanation.surface: Clean air and growing brainpower in someone from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' rearranges AIR into IRA; 'rising' turns IQ into QI.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Iraq is an Asian, as Iraq lies in western Asia.

clue.text: Lead shot originally found on pitch

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: pitch is a black sticky substance like tar

explanation.surface: A footballer's opening shot comes from the playing field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' is the black substance, not the playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: The lead in a film or play is its star performer.

clue.text: Took legal action about slur being prolonged

indicators.note: about means the word for legal action goes around the slur

parts.note: sued means took someone to court
a stain is a slur on one's character

explanation.surface: A defamation suit drags on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link; the definition is 'prolonged', describing something kept up.
explanation.definitionFit: Sustained effort is kept up continuously, that is, maintained over a long time.

clue.text: When company has time for course

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A firm finds time for a training course.
explanation.walkthrough: ASCOT is a famous English racecourse in Berkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse, home of the Royal Ascot meeting.

clue.text: Odd about duck being an extinct species

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the three letters of odd are rearranged

parts.note: in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, written O

explanation.surface: A peculiar duck said to have died out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges ODD into DOD; the duck is the cricket nought, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius died out in the seventeenth century, a byword for extinction.

clue.text: Lad likely to go wrong? Romeo, Romeo!

indicators.note: going wrong means the letters are set awry and rearranged

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A young man is likely to stray, being a Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go wrong' rearranges LIKELY into YKILLE; LAD already sits in place. The first Romeo is the radio code letter, the second the lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady-killer is a charming womaniser, as is a Romeo, after Shakespeare's lover.
